clauses.reason: Executive Order 6811 of August 4, 1934 states: "do hereby approve said Amendment and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry by Executive Order dated November 26, 1933, and my previous approval of the said Code as amended by Executive Order dated June 29, 1934, to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended" That command is a approval of an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry and modification of the earlier approvals to cover the code as amended under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and it has legal effect only through that approval: under section 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, and under sections 3(c) and 3(f) violations were restrainable in equity and punishable as misdemeanors. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no other effective date, so the command ended as a prospective operative command on June 14, 1935. No earlier end is shown (see earlier_end_check). The June 16, 1935 expiry is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced it with April 1, 1936. Schechter (295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date.

inventory_overrides.reason: Items 1 to 4 and the first part of item 5 are findings that command nothing, and item 5 also carries the final operative sentence. The corrected inventory is the single sentence that approves the amendment and modifies the earlier approvals.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6811 (August 4, 1934) is a approval of an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry and modification of the earlier approvals to cover the code as amended under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Read in full from the held American Presidency Project transcription (page record checked; identity, date and subject confirmed against the census register and the WPA 1944 list); the order's own text states no limit on the approval. Its command depends entirely on the code approval, so its first end is the repeal of the code-approval and code-enforcement provisions of Title I by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 on June 14, 1935, applying SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and its adjudication; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization only.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states no period, \"until\" date, condition or provisional approval that limits the approval, and no stay or postponement to a fixed date. Held later orders naming the code are EO 7000 (April 5, 1935) and EO 7018 (April 19, 1935); the earlier approvals are EO 6444 (November 26, 1933) and EO 6756-D (June 29, 1934). I read the operative sentence of each: each approves amendments and modifies the previous approval to include an approval of the code in its entirety as amended. None cancels, suspends, supersedes or revokes the approval, so each later order is a later event. No held text cites this order by number. No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or revoked before June 14, 1935, and none shows a modification under section 10(b) that reached this order's command. June 16, 1935 is not an end, because section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date.","independent_command_check":"No appointment, delegation, direction to a government agency, report direction or other command independent of the code approval appears. The \"Approval recommended\" and signature lines command nothing.","savings_check":"Read S.J. Res. 113 section 2 and its proviso and NIRA section 5 in the packet excerpts. No held source continues this approval, a prosecution under it or any command of this order after June 14, 1935; accrued acts, liabilities and the section 5 exemption for completed action are recorded as transferred or accrued and not as continued operation.","scope_check":"The machine inventory has five clauses, items 1 to 5, which are the President's numbered findings (application made, notice, hearings held, the code as amended complies with section 3(a), the policy of Congress) and, at the end of item 5, the final approval. Findings command nothing. The only operative command is the final sentence approving the amendment and modifying the earlier approvals, which is the single corrected clause (inventory correction recorded). The held text does not reproduce the amendment; its content is not needed because it takes effect only as a term of the code approved under section 3."}

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences, and the section 5 exemption from the antitrust laws for action complying with an approved code taken while Title I was in effect is likewise an accrued effect for completed action. The proviso to section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 names agreements and action under them, not codes, and states no time limit; the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the section 5 exemption for past action under codes, and whatever exemption survives for past action is an accrued effect, not continued operation of this approval. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval after June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495, held the code provisions in question invalid on both of its grounds; recorded as a validity characterization of section 3 code approvals, not as an end date for this order. It adjudicated the Live Poultry Code provisions and cancelled or withdrew no other approving order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: date the Act was approved; states the repealed legal effects of a code approval, not an end date
source_notes.reason: Sections 3(a)-(f) state the legal effects of an approved code that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed: the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition (3(b)), district courts could restrain violations (3(c)), and violations were misdemeanors (3(f)).
